notes: §1985:XV.3.2.4 GR24: DEBUG-LINE identifies the referencing statement, DEBUG-NAME is identifier-1's name, and "DEBUG-CONTENTS contains the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 at the time that control passes to the debugging section". DebugTriggerEmitter.FireText passes the statement line, the target name and DataItemImage of the identified place to DebugItem.PopulateReference; the witness (same/other statement DEBUG-LINE, DEBUG-NAME, contents) and probes dbg/g5, g6, g11 (30-character name, WRITE FROM contents after the move, PERFORM VARYING phases, refmod store gives the whole item) are right. The item referenced is the occurrence the statement identified: at the start of the statement (§1985:IV.4.3.8, kb/Work PB5294) or, for a receiver its statement identifies immediately before its store (§1985:VI.6.19.4 GR2, §1985:VI.6.4.6 GR2, §1985:VI.6.11.4 GR4, §1985:VI.6.23.4 GR3d, §1985:VII.4.4.4 GR8b), at that store (DebugTriggerEmitter.IdentifiedAtStore, kb/Work PB5385). Witness pb5385-debug-receiver-identified-at-store: MOVE 3 TO SUB NT (SUB) shows NT (3)'s 3, READ F INTO XE (FR-SUB) the record's 3Z in XE (3).

DEBUG-LINE identifies the source statement"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds USE FOR DEBUGGING; the 14.9.49 USE statement rules cover only exception declaratives (EXCEPTION-OBJECT).". No 2023 clause holds the Debug module. The USE rules shown cover only exception declaratives, with no debugging section and no DEBUG-LINE, DEBUG-NAME or DEBUG-CONTENTS.
